poster.note: Strong stage poster: Wren lobs an egg at Kindly's smiley moon, the only light, pink rim on her lit side, dark band (L 0.144), calm caption strip; 2:3 and 1:1 are real recompositions. Polish: the egg's highlight sits up-left, away from the smile; relight it from up-right like the marker egg.

focus.note: 0.47,0.56 keeps Wren and the egg in every wall shape, the 4:3 phone crop and the half plate. The 577x163 strip keeps only the lower half of the smile; y≈0.50 would keep its face too (optional).

icon.note: Drawn for 46, not a shrunk poster: capped head in profile with one pink rim; reads on night and linen, hard pixels, no text or scene.

emblem.note: Wren's red cap alone, fewer parts than the icon, reads as a cap (not a generic symbol) at 30 px on both grounds.

keyStill.note: Real tension: Wren holds Biscuit back as the drone's pink scan ring lands one step below; subject centred, same finish, reads at 360x176 and 132x66.

result.note: The payoff: Dolly and Wren laughing over the tarts under one pendant lamp, all inside the middle 720, no text or numbers; the stove dial's figures were painted out.

gallery.note: Six real moments in the game's renderer (fight, thank-you, steps, Biscuit, Car 17, the dozen), varied in place, scale and light, subjects in the central 4:3, only the game's in-stage HUD on 01.

seals.note: 8 moments + 1 event, three states each (27 files); ring / bus transfer / gable read apart at 32 px, one glyph each, no gold, no padlock, no text. Weakest: last-stop's lever and the low-contrast pigeon; earned vs progress is subtle at 32.

store.note: pigeon-pal (Little Pope) reads at 40 px as plain Biscuit with a speck on top, nearly the same tile as biscuit-tape; show the pigeon itself large (or a tight crop on it on the lid) so the companion is what reads.

passTile.note: 'THE LONG WAY HOME' on a transfer ticket in the game's ptext font, Wren and Biscuit on the night street; no price or count, guarded colours only as single sprite pixels.

passGrounds.note: Three clearly different world grounds (night pavement, Car 17 floor slats, Dolly's teal linoleum), no lettering, no guarded fills.

marker.note: Dolly's egg rolling (next) and sitting in a carton cup (held), drawn for 48, lit from up-right, nothing that counts.

passRewards.note: Six rewards on their row grounds, full art at rest, read at ~120 px. Tart-sticker's pale custard reads more like a bun; a warmer custard (still off sun) would help.

owned.note: 'Punched': a transfer-punch hole clipped into the tile corner, one play under 900 ms ending on the held hole; no gold or glow, the held ring is visible at 40 px.

update.note: Gus's antenna with Pilar's walkie rings, same night light and medium as the poster, no version or 'update' lettering, reads at 104x52. Only use it if the antenna ships after launch; it is already in the build (the chat flagged this).

event.note: The Long Table is visibly a different night (many neighbours, warm windows, Kindly's pod switched off), left 45% plain, subject right, distinct gable seal. The bulbs read as little bunting crosses and their light barely lands on the diners; worth strengthening.

living.note: On narrow plates (150x370 tested) the loop pans until Wren and the scooter both leave the frame and the plate shows only sky and houses; keep the anchor on Wren in every frame (bring the machine to her, or stack the fight vertically).

backdrop.note: Carmody Street at rest, every window dark, one low pink glow from off right, ends on the kerb; phone composed separately; darker than the poster, so the poster leads.

share.note: At the 270 px link preview the lockup is ~136 px wide, under its own stated minimum of 344, so 'Pardon the' in the pill drops to ~3 px and only APOCALYPSE reads; enlarge the pill (or the whole lockup) for this card. Wren's 0.08% ember-near sprite pixels are acceptable.

chip.note: Head-and-shoulders Wren raising an egg toward Kindly's glow: more parts than the icon, fewer than the poster, no text.

phone.note: A true 9:16 recomposition from the poster scene code (smile on the turret, egg mid-arc), same one image and register.

lockup.note: The game's own lettering (gloss 'Pardon the' pill over pixel APOCALYPSE) with its minimum width stated (344 px); kept off the poster.

overall: One of the strongest passes: every picture is rendered inside the real build or hand-placed in the game's code and palette, with one coherent finish (pixel people, smooth gloss for Kindly, one visible light, Bayer dither) and a poster that holds on the wall and in every shape. Three fixes before it is done: the pigeon store tile, the moving poster losing Wren on narrow plates, and the title being too small on the share card at link-preview size.
copying: none. The big pink disc behind the character recalls Gob's pink disc, but here it is Kindly's own kSmiley from the game code, the game's antagonist and colour; no moonbeam wedge, clay, ruled paper, stamps, dot whale or beams were borrowed.
made: Rendered inside the real game build via a headless-browser render script (tools/render.py) calling the game's own drawing functions (areaCanvas, personFrame, kSmiley, drawBiscuit, drawEnemy, gloss), plus new light passes written on the game's helpers; small marks, seals and some props hand-placed as pixel maps in the game's palette. The moving poster and owned mark are hand-written JS modules with baked game sprites. Seven parallel agents plus a lead.
